title: Skein allocator: targeted KV-pool sharding and fragmentation healing for GPU memory
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: long-running inference workers accumulate KV cache fragmentation on GPU memory under continuous batching workloads. When models have heterogeneous per-request sequence lengths and token churn, small free holes appear across slab pools that degrade effective capacity and increase out-of-memory (OOM) risk or force heavier evictions, causing tail-latency spikes.

Goal: implement a skein-style KV-pool allocator that shards pools by token-residency signatures and adds light-weight, targeted healing passes to reduce fragmentation without large-stop-the-world compaction. Deliver measurable reduction in fragmentation ratio, improved token residency stability, and fewer OOMs on typical PLG workloads while preserving low-latency continuous batching.
decisions: Introduce 'skein' shard key derived from token residency fingerprint + model shard ID to place allocations into localized pools.
Avoid synchronous global compaction; use opportunistic micro-healing sweeps on underutilized lanes during idle cycles.
Prefer probabilistic relocation (copy-on-write) with batched GPU kernels to amortize relocation cost rather than immediate pointer-chase remaps.
Expose a tunable 'heal_budget' per node to bound CPU/GPU impact and ensure SLOs are respected.
Integrate with batching controller so hot lanes are not healed during high QPS windows; use telemetry hints for scheduling.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype user-space skein hash function and deterministic pool assignment in a feature branch (2 wks).
Phase 2: Add lightweight per-pool free-list with hole-size bucketing, and micro-heal worker that coalesces compatible adjacent holes within a pool (3 wks).
Phase 3: GPU kernel for batched relocation of KV entries: design API for batched memcpy + kv-index update (3 wks).
Phase 4: Integrate heal_budget and batch-aware gating into scheduling; add config flags + runtime metrics (1 wk).
Phase 5: Canary rollout to Dedicated staging, monitor fragmentation and OOM signals, iterate (2 wks).
acceptance_criteria: Sustained fragmentation ratio (free_holes_weighted / total_pool) reduced by >= 35% on our synthetic churn benchmark compared to baseline.
No regression in p95 latency with continuous batching enabled (<= 3% relative change).
OOM events attributable to KV fragmentation reduced by >= 50% in canary fleet over three days.
Heal_budget default setting does not increase CPU utilization by more than 7% on our Dedicated nodes.
Feature gated by runtime flag and fully revertible with zero downtime.
telemetry_and_metrics: kv_relocation_ops: counter (batched ops and tokens moved)
p95_latency_by_model_and_pool: derived metric to detect regressions
risks: Relocation kernels could interact poorly with existing KV cache eviction and increase tail latency if not batched appropriately.
Incorrect shard heuristics might worsen hot-cold skew, creating more micro-hot pools that fragment faster.
GPU memory copies for relocation consume PCIe bandwidth and could impact concurrent inference throughput on shared hosts.
Edge cases with very short-lived tokens (high churn models) may cause thrashing—need guardrails and higher heal thresholds.
comments: 2026-02-22 — Asha Raman: Spiked a simple skein hash; observed 18% reduction in small-hole counts on localized synthetic traces. Next step: formalize pool boundaries and free-list bucketing.

2026-02-28 — Liam O'Connor: Reviewed prototype. Concern: relocation kernel will need careful tuning for models with long KV entries. Suggest adding per-entry size guard to avoid moving huge blobs during micro-heal.
2026-03-04 — Priya Menon (SRE): Recommend heal_budget default 0.05 (5% of idle cycles) and an emergency throttle if eviction rate increases > 10% over baseline.
2026-03-08 — Design review: agreed to expose 'skein_salt' per-tenant to avoid cross-tenant collision and to log pool assignment for debugging.
2026-03-10 — Liam O'Connor: Implemented per-pool hole bucketing and a first-pass GPU memcpy kernel. Running end-to-end smoke tests now.
notes: Prefer incremental rollout: staging -> 5% prod -> 25% prod -> full. Monitor kv_fragmentation_ratio and p95 latency at each step.
We should coordinate with packaging team for runtime-1.20 release notes and enablement docs for Dedicated customers.
Follow-on: evaluate combining skein allocation with adaptive batch coalescing hints from the scheduler to further reduce relocation frequency.
